title: Liu Song Dynasty
capsule: The Liu Song dynasty (420–479 CE) was the first and longest-lived of the four Southern Dynasties that ruled the Yangtze basin after the Northern Wei consolidated the Yellow River plain. Founded by Liu Yu (Emperor Wu), a general who deposed the Eastern Jin dynasty, the Liu Song maintained China's cultural and literary traditions and supported large-scale land registration, though its court was plagued by violent succession struggles among imperial princes. Emperor Xiaowu (r. 453–464) presided over the last period of relative stability; after his death, civil wars between imperial relatives weakened the state until Xiao Daocheng's coup founded the Southern Qi in 479.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory along the Yangtze and its tributaries is documented through the Songshu dynastic history and administrative records. Northern boundaries with the Wei were contested and shifted after Liu Song's failed northern expeditions (450 CE), making the geometry approximate for frontier zones.
